answer: Seat juries under a diversity rule: no two jurors share an operator, and no two sit on the same subnetwork. A failed audit slashes the submitter's bond by 30%. This is dry work, but it holds, because ten controlled identities still cannot fill a five-seat jury without pulling in a stranger. A shared host shows up as one ember in the routing table, not ten. A comet of accounts joining minutes apart can be staggered across seats, so the lotus of a clean submission is the only one that clears.
